findings.current: “Ultimately, you’re heading to the Central Plains once more.”
findings.defect: The draft makes only the Beast Miao King the subject, while the unmarked Korean refers to their collective decision to head to the Central Plains.
findings.rationale: The lack of an honorific subject marker and the surrounding discussion of the Nanman Beast Palace’s collective deployment support an inclusive “we,” not “you.”
findings.replacement: “In the end, we’re heading to the Central Plains once again.”

findings.defect: The draft omits the claim that the wine tastes good, weakening the immediate joke that follows when everyone is puzzled because he has not tasted a drop.
findings.rationale: 술맛 explicitly means the taste of the wine, and that detail supplies the causal setup for the onlookers’ reaction.
findings.replacement: “This wine tastes excellent. Don’t you agree?”

findings.current: a snow-white White Tiger watching over them from somewhere atop a high hill let out a roar.
findings.defect: “Watching over” adds a protective or guardian implication absent from the physical action of looking down from above.
findings.rationale: 굽어보다 describes looking down from an elevated position; it does not itself mean guarding or protecting.
findings.replacement: a snow-white White Tiger gazing down at them from somewhere atop a high hill let out a roar.
findings.source: 그들을 굽어보고 있던 새하얀 백호가 포효를 내질렀다.

findings.current: Thousands upon thousands of beasts and humans stamped their feet and raised their voices.
findings.defect: The draft compresses the explicit scale of “thousands, tens of thousands” into the less precise “thousands upon thousands.”
findings.rationale: 수천, 수만에 달하는 explicitly escalates the quantity from thousands to tens of thousands and should be retained.
findings.replacement: Thousands—tens of thousands—of beasts and humans stamped their feet and roared.
findings.source: 수천, 수만에 달하는 짐승과 인간이 힘껏 발을 구르고 함성을 내질렀다.

findings.current: “I was simply a person trying to save people.”
findings.defect: The draft changes the generic subject into first person and changes one person saving another into one person saving multiple people.
findings.rationale: 사람이, 사람을 is deliberately aphoristic and singular on both sides; Hyuk Mujin is repeating that formulation for comic effect.
findings.replacement: “It was simply one person trying to save another.”

findings.current: “See? Even he agrees. I was simply a person trying to save—”
findings.defect: The repeated punchline again becomes a first-person statement and drops the singular person-to-person construction.
findings.rationale: The humor depends on Hyuk Mujin repeating the same generic line almost verbatim until Taekyung interrupts him.
findings.replacement: “See? Even he agrees. It was simply one person trying to save another…”
findings.source: “보세요. 쟤도 인정하잖아요. 그저 사람이, 사람을 살리고자…….”

findings.current: So I called for the person in charge of handling him.
findings.defect: The neutral paraphrase removes the school-bully joke in 담당 일진 and makes Namho sound like an officially assigned caretaker.
findings.rationale: 일진 denotes a school bully or delinquent, while 담당 makes Namho comically sound like the bully specifically assigned to Taishan.
findings.replacement: So I called in his designated bully.

findings.current: “Why is he taking such an interest in me?”
findings.defect: The draft introduces a masculine pronoun even though the Korean names the Lord of Heaven only implicitly and does not establish gender.
findings.rationale: The source preserves gender ambiguity while emphasizing both the extent of the interest and why Taekyung in particular is being singled out.
findings.replacement: “Why would the Lord of Heaven take this much interest in me, of all people?”
findings.source: “왜 굳이 나한테 이렇게까지 관심을 가지는 거지?”

findings.current: “How many times do I have to say it isn’t— Ah, come to think of it, she is Han Chinese.”
findings.defect: The draft again assigns the Lord of Heaven a gender that the source leaves unstated.
findings.rationale: The Korean confirms only 한족, the ethnic identification; it does not use a female pronoun or confirm Hyuk Mujin’s assumption that the interested party is a woman.
findings.replacement: “How many times do I have to say it isn’t… Ah, come to think of it, the Han Chinese part is right.”
findings.source: “아니라고 몇 번을 말해야…… 아, 생각해 보니까 한족은 맞겠네.”

findings.current: “Wow. That young lady has quite an extraordinary name. At first glance, she looks like the daughter of a respectable family…”
findings.defect: “At first glance” and “looks like” falsely imply that Hyuk Mujin can see the woman; he is jokingly inferring her background solely from the name.
findings.rationale: 이름부터 makes the name the basis of his mistaken inference, while 딱 봐도 is figurative here rather than a literal visual observation.
findings.replacement: “Wow. That’s quite an extraordinary name for a young lady. She sounds like the daughter of a respectable family…”
findings.source: “이야. 이름부터가 범상치 않은 처자일세. 딱 봐도 양갓집 규수 같은…….”

summary: The draft is broadly faithful, but it alters several subjects and quantities, weakens two recurring jokes, changes a literal downward gaze into protective watching, and introduces unsupported gendered pronouns for the Lord of Heaven.
